cards.text: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus, is writing to the believers in Ephesus, and here he reminds them where they started. Not sick, not sleepy, friend: dead in their trespasses and sins. Back then they walked in those sins.

cards.question: Paul says that back when the believers in Ephesus walked in their sins, they were just following their own way and nobody else's.

cards.text: No, they were going along with the ways of this world and of the ruler of the power of the air, the spirit now at work in the sons of disobedience. Then Paul describes a whole way of life: fulfilling the cravings of the flesh and indulging its desires and thoughts. That's a craving holding the car keys, baker.

cards.question: Who does Paul say lived that way at one time, fulfilling the cravings of the flesh?

cards.text: Then comes the hardest line yet: "Like the rest, we were by nature children of wrath." That's not one burnt edge, friend, that's the whole batch right from the dough, but then Paul writes "But" and God steps in because of His great love for us.

cards.question: God steps in for people who were by nature children of wrath. Paul calls Him a God who is rich in ___.

cards.text: God doesn't patch us up or hand us a pep talk. He made us alive with Christ.

cards.question: Paul says God waited until we had cleaned up our lives, and then He made us alive with Christ.

cards.text: Then Paul bursts out, "It is by grace you have been saved!" And he keeps going: God raised us up with Christ.

cards.question: After God raised us up with Christ, where does Paul say God seated us?

answers.text: With Him in the heavenly realms

cards.text: And Paul tells why God did all this, friend: so that in the coming ages He might put something on display.

cards.question: Paul says God did all this so that in the coming ages He could show off how hard His people worked.

cards.text: No, it's the surpassing riches of His grace, shown by His kindness to us in Christ Jesus. Then that grace line comes back, and this time Paul adds that it's through faith. Then he says this is not from yourselves.

cards.question: Paul says, "and this not from yourselves; it is the ___ of God."

cards.text: And it's not by works, either. Good news for me, friend: I stamped crooked cookies for YEARS in a junk drawer, and if it came down to my work, I'd still be stuck behind the takeout menus.

cards.question: Paul says being saved is not by works. What does that mean no one can do?

cards.text: So do good works even matter? Paul says we are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus, and let me tell you, baker, God doesn't stamp crooked.

cards.question: We are God's workmanship, created in Christ Jesus. What does Paul say we were created to do?

answers.text: Good works God prepared in advance
Good works that earn His grace
Good works that pay off our sins
